chapter_theme: How hard it is to restrain the five senses (ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் அருமை): the senses are rutting elephants that tire the mahout, a horse no learning can steer, birds and lions feeding in five fields; the poet confesses he cannot conquer them, though cutting their claws and teeth would bring one to the Lord.
structure_note: A sequence of animal images for the senses (elephants, a leaping horse, birds, lions), the five as rulers with ninety-six ministers, a personal confession (2028), and a closing verse on great powers that stands apart.

2023.reading: There are five elephants in rut within the body; they do not come to the post of the Agamas' teaching; once the mahout is spent and they too have weakened, we do not know how to set yoga right by uniting.
2023.nuance: ஆக மதத்தன puns on ஆகம் (body) and மதம் (rut), and ஆக மதத் தறி on ஆகமம் (scripture) and தறி (tethering post). The mahout is commonly taken as the mind or the self. The last line admits defeat rather than prescribing.

2024.reading: Though the mahout has learned good books in his mind and jabs with his foot to correct it, the leaping beast only leaps in confusion; even if he climbs onto its neck and sits there and goads it, that beast will not keep to the road.
2024.nuance: பாய்மா (the leaping beast) is usually a horse; எருத்து (neck) suits an elephant or bull, so the beast may continue 2023's elephants. The point is that book learning does not tame the senses.

2025.reading: Five fields, five birds, and the birds go and feed there; five lands, five waters, five natures; one family, and one herdsman tends them with a staff; and the ways by which they come and go are nine.
2025.nuance: The fives are traditionally the senses, their objects and their qualities, and the nine ways the body's nine openings. The herdsman may be the soul or the Lord. The verse lays out the scheme without stating a moral.

2026.reading: Five lions live in the forest; the five go out to feed and come back into their five dens; if the claws and teeth of the five are cut, reaching the Lord fully becomes possible.
2026.nuance: The lions are the senses and their dens the sense organs, as the image is usually read. Cutting claws and teeth disarms the senses without killing them.

2027.reading: Under the five ministers are ninety-six; the five and their sons mean to rule; if the five stand with their anger, we cannot pay the tribute to the five.
2027.nuance: தொண்ணூற்று அறுவர் is traditionally the ninety-six tattvas of an extended count. சிறை இறுத்து may be 'paying the levy' or 'breaking the prison'; the second would reverse the sense of the last line.

2028.reading: Day after day I cannot speak of the radiant light, nor of the holy lady who is there too; I cannot conquer the five senses and myself; I have become like a horse that bolts when one stands to strike it.
2028.nuance: திருமங்கை (the holy lady) is commonly taken as Shakti, with the light as Siva. கொல்ல நின்று ஓடும் குதிரை may also be a horse that runs on to its death. A rare first-person confession of failure.

2029.reading: Shut that pot of countless holes in the dark room; going along with it brings error; if one guards against going along with it, there is bliss.
2029.nuance: எண்ணிலி இல்லி is read here as a pot pierced with countless holes, an old image for the leaking body or mind; this is a guess. The verse repeats எண்ணிலி இல்லி in every line and the last line (இல்லதோடு) may mean 'with the one who has no holes'.

2030.reading: The great strength of fate is the sea-girt earth; the great strength of praise is the ancient heaven; the great strength of the mind is human life; the great strength of wealth is the strength of water.
2030.nuance: Each line pairs a power with its domain, but the logic is unclear, and மதி may be mind or the moon. The verse seems to stand apart from the chapter's senses.

links.note: Both picture the senses as five elephants to be controlled. The Kural says the one who guards them with the goad of firmness is a seed for release; Tirumular shows the mahout exhausted and confesses he does not know how to manage it. The goal agrees; the confidence that it can be done does not.
Two animal images for the same discipline: the Kural's tortoise draws its five limbs in; Tirumular's five lions go out to feed and must have claws and teeth cut. Withdrawal against disarming.

Both count five senses and the gates through which craving comes and goes, and make guarding them the way to release; the Naladiyar names the five gates, Tirumular adds the nine openings and a herdsman.
2024 shows a mahout who cannot steer the leaping beast; in 2028 the poet says he himself has become that unruly horse.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate; Tirumular gives fate's great strength the earth but assigns heaven to praise and human life to the mind, so fate is one power among several. The tension depends on reading 2030's domains as limits.

2026 says five lions live in the forest (அஞ்சுள சிங்கம் அடவியுள் வாழ்வன) and reaching the Lord is possible once their claws and teeth are cut; 977 opens the same way with five elephants (அஞ்சுள ஆனை அடவியுள் வாழ்வன) and makes the five letters their goad. The same frame gives two methods: disarming the senses in 2026, steering them with the mantra in 977.

2027 names five ministers with ninety-six (தொண்ணூற்று அறுவர்) under them who mean to rule; 2146 counts the ninety-six instruments of the first state: elements, senses, malas, gunas and adharas. 2146 supplies the list behind 2027's court, so the five senses' ninety-six servants are the tattvas.

2029 bids one shut the pot of countless holes (எண்ணிலி இல்லி) in the dark room and not go along with it; Naladiyar 47 calls the body a pot (கும்பம்) seeping through nine openings that the fool praises. If இல்லி is the perforated pot, both picture the body as a leaking vessel: the Naladiyar to cure desire for it, the Tirumanthiram to bid its openings closed. The reading of 2029 is uncertain.

source_issues: 2029 is obscure throughout (எண்ணிலி இல்லி, இல்லதோடு) and may be corrupt.
2027 line 4: சிறைஇறுத்து may be read as 'paying tribute' or 'breaking prison', with opposite senses.
